html:
The Mechoopda are a tribe of Maidu people of the Sacramento Valley in California, at today's city of Chico. They historically spoke Konkow, a language related to Maidu.

Their village stood where the Gold Rush settler John Bidwell set up his Rancho Chico in the late 1840s. Bidwell hired them as workers, and the village became a rancheria on his land, which gave them some shelter during the violence of the Gold Rush years. The tribe lost federal status in the 1960s and later won it back. They are enrolled in the Mechoopda Indian Tribe of Chico Rancheria. Their neighbours include the Konkow and the Mountain Maidu.
